title: Orthogonality of distinct characters
statement: Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$, and let $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$. For $s, t \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$ with $s \ne t$, the Fourier characters $\chi_s(x) = \omega_k^{s\cdot x}$ and $\chi_t(x) = \omega_k^{t\cdot x}$ are orthogonal with respect to the Hermitian inner product $\langle f, g\rangle = \frac{1}{k^n}\sum_{x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n} f(x)\,\overline{g(x)}$; that is, $\langle \chi_s, \chi_t\rangle = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: s and t are vectors in Z_k^n
replaced:
If $s \neq t$, then $\langle \chi_s, \chi_t \rangle = 0$.
Together with $\texttt{ZkFourier.inner\_product\_char\_self}$, this shows that the
characters form an orthonormal system.
